findings.title: Contract-v7 peers silently discard the new retry-failure fields
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:108 — CONTRACT_VERSION remains 7 although crates/blit-core/proto/blit.proto:285 adds ManifestComplete.scan_failures, and negotiation accepts different builds solely by matching this version.
findings.predicted_failure: During a rolling upgrade, a pre-change v7 receiver ignores the new protobuf fields. A retry whose requested file is not enumerated can therefore return a zero-failure summary, causing the new initiator to discard the original failure and report success; a destructive move can consequently delete a source file that never landed.
findings.better_approach: Bump the session contract version and document the new semantics, or negotiate an explicit scan-failure capability and refuse/fail conservatively when the peer lacks it.

findings.title: Unnamed scan failures can disappear after another retry
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:292 — record_unnamed_failures increments only files_failed_total; wire_failed_paths later returns truncated=false when its named paths fit, and crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/retry.rs:88 consequently treats that incomplete nonempty path list as exact.
findings.predicted_failure: If ManifestComplete.scan_failures exceeds its 1 MiB budget, omitted failures are counted but the summary claims its retry path set is complete. With another retry pass, only named paths are retried; if those converge, after_pass replaces the state with a clean result and the omitted files vanish from the failure count, producing exit 0 despite files never landing.
findings.better_approach: Track unnamed-path presence in SinkOutcome and force failed_paths_truncated whenever files_failed_total exceeds the represented path identities; carry that unretried count forward until positively resolved.

findings.title: Lossy-name collisions shield only one physical destination path
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/mirror_planner.rs:300 — shield construction uses raw_entries.iter().find for a lossy text identity, even though multiple distinct raw paths can collapse to that same text.
findings.predicted_failure: On a byte-keyed destination, two non-UTF-8 source names can share one lossy text path. When one is rejected as the duplicate and its destination is a populated directory, the shield may resolve to the other raw name; mirror deletion then removes descendants beneath the failed entry even though that subtree was required to remain untouched.
findings.better_approach: Carry the failed entry's structured raw identity into mirror planning. At minimum, conservatively shield the textual identity and every raw entry sharing that text instead of selecting the first match.
